method:
Driver sensitivity table (Kilian 2026-11-09, replaces the assumption grade).
For each driver of a name's live driver set that has a measured history:
  annual change c_t = ln(x_t / x_t-1) for levels, x_t - x_t-1 for fractions (history: data/driver_history_*.json)
  half-width per year  hw = max(2 sd(c), max |c_t - mean c|)   (covers every past annual move, and at least 2 sd)
  a forecast quarter j quarters past the last reported one is moved by hw * sqrt(j/4) (uncertainty grows with horizon):
    levels x * exp(+-hw sqrt(h)), fractions x +- hw sqrt(h)
  low/high research target (12m) = engine re-run with the whole forecast path of that one driver at its low/high path.
  elast_pct per driver-year = % move in the target per +1% (levels) or +1pt (fractions) in that year's forecast quarters.

rows.label: Capital expenditures (purchases of property and equipment)
Google Cloud revenue per $ of Cloud-share server stock (annualized, ex TPU license fees)
rows.range_reason: Revenue per $ of Cloud server stock rose 0.81 -> 1.11 over seven quarters (filed Cloud revenue / derived stock); we hold 1.107. High = extend the 2025-26 rise (~+0.02/qtr); low = the model's -10% bear (price per unit of compute falling faster than compute per $ rises). Overlap: Cloud capacity revenue = stock x cloud_share x cloud_yield, so this row and cloud_share move the same product (revenue per $ of servers) from different evidence (pricing vs allocation); each row holds the other fixed, but the combined sigma assumes they are independent, and a lower Cloud share could hold prices up (negative correlation), so the GOOGL total may slightly overstate. Outside (11-10): Street 2027 revenue $626.8B mean vs our $618.0B; if the gap is all Cloud, Cloud is ~$206B vs our $197B (yield ~1.16). The Street spread is $545-715B (50 analysts), too wide to use its ends as Cloud points; no published 2027 Cloud consensus found.

rows.label: Realized fuel, purchased power and delivery cost (ex nuclear fuel amortization)
rows.range_reason: Range follows gas. Gas is 62% of capacity and 54% of 2025 output (112.7 of 207.2 TWh, 10-K segment tables), and Henry Hub annual averages moved about -15% to +50% a year in 2023-26 (EIA). Gas at ~60% of fuel cost x a ~+-30% gas move = ~+-18% a year: FY27 +-12%, FY28 +-18%, FY29 +-20%. The gas price also moves the power price, and the row now moves both together. The 98%/78% hedge figures cover power sold (10-K Item 7A: gas hedges are used as a proxy for power-price exposure, and fuel is bought spot and near term, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1692819/000169281926000006/vistra-20251231.htm). So on the hedged slice, realized power price stays fixed and the fuel move is a pure margin squeeze. On the unhedged slice (FY26 0%, FY27 2%, FY28 22%, FY29 ~50% as in gen_price), power price moves with gas: each $1/MWh of fleet fuel change moves the unhedged power price by $1.11/MWh (= 0.60 gas share of fuel / 0.54 gas share of output, i.e. the price-setting gas unit passes its fuel cost through at Vistra's own gas-fleet heat rate). That pass-through is a convention, not a disclosed number; a higher market heat rate would pass through more and narrow the range further. Outside (11-10, MarketScreener roundup 2026-10-27): Henry Hub 2027 EIA $3.16, NYMEX strip $3.13, BofA $4.00, Enverus $3.25 vs 2026 $3.48; 2028-30 strip ~$3.65-3.70. Converted to fuel $/MWh as 25.97 x (1 + 0.6 x gas change), holding non-gas fuel flat: FY27 24.5-28.3, FY28 ~26.9. Note: the model's FY28 fuel (28.93, +11%) sits above the strip-implied ~26.9; worth a look at the next VST update.
